question: A cone has height h and radius r. The cone is melted and recast into a smaller cone whose height is (h)/(2) and radius is (r)/(3). What fraction of the original volume is unused?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any cone, Volume ∝ r² × h.

New radius is 1/3 of the original, and new height is 1/2 of the original.

Ratio of new volume to original volume = (1/3)² × (1/2) = 1/9 × 1/2 = 1/18.

This means 1 part of the original volume is used out of 18 total parts.

Unused fraction = 1 − 1/18 = 17/18.

**∴ The correct answer is 17/18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Original cone height = h, radius = r

New smaller cone height = h/2, radius = r/3

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cone = 1/3 × π × radius² × height

**Calculations:**

Let the volume of the original cone be V₁.

⇒ V₁ = 1/3 × π × r² × h

Let the volume of the new smaller cone be V₂.

⇒ V₂ = 1/3 × π × (r/3)² × (h/2)

⇒ V₂ = 1/3 × π × (r² / 9) × (h/2)

⇒ V₂ = (1/18) × (1/3 × π × r² × h)

⇒ V₂ = V₁ / 18

This means the new recast cone uses only 1/18th of the original volume.

Unused volume = Original volume − Used volume

⇒ Unused volume = V₁ − V₁ / 18

⇒ Unused volume = 17/18 × V₁

**∴ The correct answer is 17/18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of Frustum of a Cone

When a cone is cut by a plane parallel to its base, the remaining solid is called a frustum. Volume = 1/3 × π × h × (R² + r² + R × r).

Melting and Recasting Principle

When a 3D solid is melted and recast into a different shape, the total volume remains constant unless some specific portion is explicitly stated as wasted or unused.

Scaling Factor in 3D Objects

If all linear dimensions of a standard 3D solid are uniformly scaled by a factor 'k', its total surface area is scaled by k² and its volume is scaled by k³.
